title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
blurb: Showed that a model trained to predict the noise added to an image, then run as a long reverse chain, produces samples competitive with GANs.
intro: The forward process adds Gaussian noise over $T$ steps on a fixed schedule, and has a closed form for jumping from $x_0$ straight to any $x_t$. A network learns to predict the added noise with a plain mean-squared error, and sampling runs the reverse chain from pure noise, removing predicted noise and adding a little fresh noise at each step. The steps build the schedule, the forward jump, the posterior, the loss, the timestep embedding and both algorithms; the capstone trains a toy model and samples from it.
